title: Handle statewide CHM false-zero nodata cells
description:
The inspected statewide DTM/DSM assets do not declare header nodata and contain -9999 fill. Where both inputs contain fill, the published CHM computed as DSM minus DTM contains 0.0, which the current viewer preserves as valid canopy height. This can overstate valid CHM coverage and display false bare-ground values.

## Context
Found during the 2026-10-13 primary-source review in docs/werk-data/source-review.md. Current browser cleanValue masks declared nodata, values within 0.05 of -9999, and negative CHM only. DTM/DSM and CHM are on the same Group A grid in inspected statewide products. This is a user-visible source-data limitation, not permission to change source values silently.
acceptance_criteria: Validate the fill-derived CHM zero behavior on the current source assets and determine an authoritative validity mask or source correction with the publisher; if a reliable mask is available, apply it without removing genuine zero-height cells; if not, expose the ambiguity in viewer output/statistics and retain provenance; add regression tests distinguishing genuine zero CHM from fill-derived zero; do not use a blanket zero mask.
notes: Implemented in both viewers: CHM reads aligned DTM/DSM windows, verifies matching grids, and masks cells where either input is non-finite, declared nodata, or within 0.05 of -9999. Valid zeros are retained. Synthetic tests cover paired fill, individual missing inputs, valid zeros, mismatched grids, and export provenance; a live bounded WERK probe passed. This handles the confirmed fill-derived false-zero case, not unrelated unknown source artifacts.
close_reason: CHM previews now derive validity from aligned DTM/DSM inputs and preserve true zero-height cells; limitations and provenance are documented.

title: Show acquisition coverage and campaign context
description:
Help users see where raster values have valid coverage and which lidar acquisition year or campaign contributed them, rather than interpreting the statewide mosaic as one uniform survey.

## Context
Value rank 3. The app has an acquisition-year raster but does not currently show coverage and year as linked context. The campaign GeoPackage is mentioned in the ingestion assessment but has not yet been verified for use.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle a coverage view and inspect acquisition-year values for the selected extent; missing pixels are distinguishable from valid zero values; campaign footprints are displayed only after the publisher footprint data has been inspected and validated; labels state that acquisition year is provenance, not a time series.

title: Compare WERK products on a shared extent
description:
Let users compare two WERK products over the same geographic extent to reveal how terrain, canopy height, cover, and height statistics relate spatially.

## Context
Value rank 2. The current viewer displays one product at a time. Keep acquisition year distinct from a temporal time series, and do not imply that values from different products are directly comparable without their units and display scales.
acceptance_criteria: Users can select two supported products and compare them with a swipe control or linked panes; map navigation stays synchronized; each legend identifies its product, units, and color range; the interface states whether color ranges are shared or independent; only the required raster windows are loaded.

title: Add native-resolution AOI exports
description:
Allow users to export a small area of interest in the source grid and CRS for analysis instead of being limited to the existing resampled EPSG:3857 preview download.

## Context
Value rank 1. The current browser export is a nearest-neighbor-resampled display preview, not a native 30 m analysis extract. Verify the raster contract and bounded-read limits per product before describing the export as analysis-ready.
acceptance_criteria: A user can export a validated AOI from supported products at native grid resolution; the output preserves source CRS, affine transform, nodata mask, and source values; acquisition-year and provenance are included where available; unsupported or oversized requests fail with an actionable message; preview downloads remain explicitly labeled as resampled previews.

title: Add selected 10 m and 1 m WERK products
description:
Extend the browser viewer beyond the current statewide 30 m inventory to useful 10 m products and selected 1 m campaign products, while retaining bounded remote access.

## Context
Value rank 9. The ingestion assessment estimates roughly 271 GB for the named statewide 10 m products and identifies separate 1 m campaign collections. Expand selectively only after metadata and grid verification.
acceptance_criteria: A documented initial subset of 10 m and selected 1 m products is available for selection; source resolution and campaign identity are accurate in the UI; each selected product passes bounded header, CRS/grid, nodata, and overview checks; requests remain windowed and have explicit size limits; no statewide bulk mirroring is required.

title: Add shareable map-view URLs
description:
Allow users to share a link that reopens a selected product and geographic view with the same display settings.

## Context
Value rank 7. The viewer is a static GitHub Pages app and currently keeps these settings only in the page state.
acceptance_criteria: A generated URL encodes the selected supported product, validated bounds, and relevant display settings; opening it restores the view; invalid or unknown parameters fall back to a safe documented default with visible feedback; URLs contain no credentials or private data.

title: Expand point inspection across products
description:
Make it easier to investigate a map location by showing values and provenance for multiple selected WERK products instead of only the current product sample.

## Context
Value rank 6. The existing map click reports only the displayed preview pixel. Do not imply native 30 m sampling when the point comes from a resampled preview.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a location presents coordinates and values for the selected products, units, acquisition year where available, and nodata status; each value is identified as a preview or native sample; additional reads are bounded and failures are shown explicitly; changing products or extent cannot leave stale values presented as current.

title: Add optional data-quality and coverage diagnostics
description:
Expose documented source limitations and missing-data patterns through optional diagnostic overlays or masks without silently changing the source raster values.

## Context
Value rank 5. Publisher caveats include high DSM/CHM outliers and terrain interpolation artifacts near water. The ingestion assessment explicitly warns against removing legitimate extremes or asserting unmeasured thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Users can view a missing-data/coverage diagnostic and toggle any quality mask that has a documented, testable basis; each mask explains its criteria and affected products; unvalidated artifact thresholds are not presented as authoritative corrections; unmasked source values remain available and unchanged.

title: Add regional raster summaries
description:
Provide useful summaries of WERK values within the chosen area, including distributions and valid-pixel coverage, beyond the current preview median and finite-pixel percentage.

## Context
Value rank 4. Current summary metrics describe a resampled preview, which should not be presented as native-resolution regional analysis. Variable definitions and acquisition timing caveats remain visible.
acceptance_criteria: For a selected supported product and extent, the app displays a distribution view and documented summary statistics; the interface identifies whether values were computed from preview pixels or native cells; analysis-grade summaries use native-resolution values; nodata is excluded and valid zero values are retained; large requests respect explicit resource limits.

title: Add accessible map color controls
description:
Improve interpretation of raster layers for people with color-vision deficiencies and users who need clearer distinction between cyclic and continuous variables.

## Context
Value rank 11. The current app assigns palettes by product family, including a rainbow palette for aspect and acquisition year.
acceptance_criteria: Users can choose from tested accessible palettes; aspect uses a cyclic palette that does not imply a false endpoint; legend ticks and units remain legible and accurate; nodata remains visually distinct; palette changes affect rendering only and do not alter exported raster values.

title: Track source inventory and health
description:
Create a reconciled inventory for the viewer's source rasters and a lightweight way to identify missing, moved, or changed assets.

## Context
Value rank 10. The ingestion assessment records known STAC inventory inconsistencies and recommends reconciling the catalog with actual directory listings. Keep original remote rasters as the source of truth unless a separate mirroring decision is made.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned manifest records each supported product's source URL, resolution, variable or band definition, license, and retrieval metadata; automated checks report unreachable sources and changed validators without treating ETags as content checksums; missing or changed sources produce actionable output; prior manifest history remains available.

title: Organize and explain the product catalog
description:
Make the 22 available raster choices easier to discover by grouping related products and explaining their meanings and interpretation limits.

## Context
Value rank 8. Avoid implying that percentiles are recalculated from all lidar returns inside the selected area; these are published raster products.
acceptance_criteria: Products are grouped into understandable categories such as terrain, canopy cover, height statistics, and acquisition provenance; every product has a concise definition and verified unit; first-return versus all-return cover and percentile interpretation are explained; keyboard users can navigate the catalog.
